title: Greener choices on a budget
description: Being greener does not require expensive products — the cheapest changes are often the greenest.

body.heading: Free and green overlap
paragraphs: Using less energy, wasting less food, walking short journeys, and keeping things longer are all free — and they are among the most effective green actions available to anyone.
Beware the idea that green living means buying a new set of special products. Replacing working things with 'eco' versions usually costs money and resources for little gain.

body.heading: Spend where it counts
paragraphs: If you do spend, spend on durability and repair: a bottle that lasts years, shoes that can be resoled, a bike that gets maintained. Cost per use applies to green choices too.
Second-hand is a green superpower: clothes, furniture, books, and electronics all carry a much smaller footprint when they are pre-loved.

body.heading: Progress, not perfection
paragraphs: Nobody lives a zero-impact life, and guilt is a poor motivator. Pick the green habits that fit your life and budget, keep them, and add another when you are ready.

takeaway: The greenest choices are usually the free ones: use less, keep things longer, buy second-hand.
